text: Handoff specifications should make states and responsive behavior explicit. The developers interviewed by zeroheight describe missing intermediate-width behavior, long-content rules, and empty states; Figma’s guide describes component documentation that includes variants and states. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Mila Cann argues against discrete handoffs in agile teams because they imply design is finished; Cegid instead uses handoff to mean a transition into shared implementation responsibility. These are explicitly attributed process framings, not evidence that implementation documentation should be eliminated. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Make implementation-ready work distinguishable from drafts and experiments. Figma describes separating work by readiness; zeroheight records developer difficulty identifying the authoritative design among experiments. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Keep designers and developers engaged during delivery. Cegid recommends resolving implementation edge cases together; Figma describes early, frequent sharing as a way to obtain feedback before the end of the process. These are practitioner recommendations, not quantified causal estimates. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Modeinspect recommends actionable QA findings that record location, expected value, observed value, severity, and a screenshot. When an engineer fixes a finding through a comment or ticket, its workflow includes a second designer review of the updated build. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: GDS recommends accessibility acceptance criteria that are specific, testable, and expressed as outcomes rather than prescribed solutions. In its method, criteria preserve earlier accessibility decisions and evolve when implementation or testing reveals missing needs. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: GOV.UK explicitly cautions that accessibility acceptance criteria alone do not make a service accessible; use them to preserve accessibility decisions across iterations rather than treating a completed checklist as sufficient assurance. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Handoff documentation should preserve the problem and decision context, rather than conveying only final screens: Figma describes a spec containing iterations, problem definitions, research links, and documentation; developers interviewed by zeroheight report missing the reasons and trade-offs behind designs. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: NN/g explicitly cautions that not every interface inconsistency is UX debt: temporary intentional variations, such as an experiment, can be acceptable when they do not cause user problems. This scopes debt triage to experience harm rather than treating every visual difference as a defect. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Nielsen Norman Group defines DesignOps as coordinating people, processes, and craft to increase design impact at scale; its operational remit includes documenting delivery processes and defining design quality and completion criteria. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Preserve design rationale alongside the implementation reference: Figma’s handoff guide describes linking specs to problem definitions, research, and iterations; Cegid recommends recording important implementation decisions and trade-offs for future work. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Define implementation-review responsibilities explicitly. The designer-developer collaboration review reports unclear responsibility boundaries and loss of UX involvement in development decisions; Cegid advocates joint decisions on emerging edge cases and review of implemented features before QA. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Modeinspect proposes a concrete design-QA workflow: the screen’s designer reviews the preview build before merge, while the engineer reviews code and retains the merge gate. Its checklist extends beyond layout to interaction states, responsive behavior, accessibility, content, and motion. This is a vendor’s proposed division of work, not a universal ownership rule. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: In Modeinspect’s distinction, visual regression compares a build with an approved previous-build baseline, whereas design QA compares the implementation with design intent; an unchanged baseline can therefore preserve an original design mismatch. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Treat implementation feedback as continuing design work: Cegid recommends joint user-story review, edge-case decisions, and feedback in both directions; Figma’s guide describes early developer collaboration and visibility into the iterations behind design decisions. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Nielsen Norman Group recommends recording UX debt and prioritizing it by user impact, frequency, journey location, and effort. Its alternatives include a labelled backlog or a separate prioritization sheet, followed by deliberate capacity for repayment; the article acknowledges that teams may consciously accept debt for release constraints. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Specify behavior beyond the default screen, including empty states and behavior between screen widths. The developer interviews identify these gaps, and Modeinspect identifies missing states and responsive decisions as sources of implementation drift. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Cegid recommends recording important implementation trade-offs so later iterations retain the reasoning, and reviewing implemented features before QA to catch accessibility, interaction, and usability issues. (low confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: A delivery feedback loop should combine implementation feedback with experience review: Cegid describes developers surfacing technical opportunities and designers spotting usability issues; NN/g recommends recurring product-team reviews and using user feedback to uncover UX debt. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA

text: Do not equate documented criteria or stable screenshots with complete quality assurance. GDS warns that accessibility acceptance criteria alone do not make a service accessible; Modeinspect warns that visual regression can preserve a baseline that never matched the intended design. (medium confidence)
keywords: DesignOps, developer handoff and design QA
